**Hydrogen – A Quick‑Reference Overview** | Category | Key Properties & Facts | |----------|------------------------| | **Basic Identity** | • Element #: 1
• Symbol: H
• Group 1, Period 1 (alkali metals family)
• Only element whose atoms contain a single proton (protium) | | **Atomic Structure** | • Electron config: [He] 1s¹ (ground state)
• Nuclear charge: +1
• First ionisation energy: 13.598 eV (1315 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Standard State (STP)** | • Colourless, odourless, tasteless diatomic gas (H₂)
• Density: 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈8.99×10⁻² g cm⁻³)
• Melting point: –259.16 °C (18.15 K)
• Boiling point: –253.00 °C (20.27 K)
• Viscosity: 8.76 µPa·s (at 25 °C)
• Specific gravity vs. N₂: 0.0737 | | **Thermodynamic Data** | • Enthalpy of formation (ΔH_f°): 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition for elemental form)
• Entropy (S°): 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹
• Heat capacity (Cp,mol): 28.84 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (ideal-gas value at 298 K) | | **Bonding & Reactivity** | • Molecular bond strength (H–H): 435.93 kJ mol⁻¹ (dissociation energy)
• Oxidation states: –1 (hydride), +1 (most common in organic chemistry)
• Acidic behaviour: weak acid when bonded to heteroatoms (pKa ~ 35 for HF); basic when forming hydrides (NaH, CaH₂)…
• Combustion: 2 H₂(g)+O₂(g)→2 H₂O(l) ΔH°≈–483.6 kJ mol⁻¹ | | **Spectroscopy** | • Rotational spectrum shows two species: *ortho* (parallel spins) and *parahydrogen* (antiparallel)*—important in NMR and astrochemistry.
• Fundamental vibrational frequency ν₀≈4401 cm⁻¹ (for H₂). | | **Isotopes** | • **Protium** ‑ ^1H (stable, natural abundance >99.98%)
• **Deuterium** ‑ ^2H (heavy hydrogen, 1n extra, ρ≈2×protium; used in spectroscopy, catalysis, nuclear reactors)
• **Tritium** ‑ ^3H (radioactive, t½≈12.32 yr, β⁻ emitter; used in self‑lighting devices, fusion research) | | **Industrial Uses** | • Ammonia synthesis (Haber–Bosch) – 30 % of global H₂ consumption.
• Methane reforming / steam methane reforming (SMR) – primary route to syngas.
• Electrolytic splitting of water – clean H₂ source for green fuel.
• Metal hydride batteries, catalytic converters, polymer manufacturing (ethylene glycol, polyethylene terephthalate).
• Cryogenics – liquid H₂ used as coolant for superconductors. | | **Energy Applications** | • Fuel cell technology (PEMFC, SOFC) – produces electricity + water from H₂/O₂.
• Rocket propellant – LH₂/LOX gives highest specific impulse (~450 s).
• Potential fusion fuel (D/T mix) – central goal of ITER and other tokamak projects. | | **Astronomical Significance** | • Most abundant element (>74 % by mass in Universe).
• Core of stellar nucleosynthesis: proton–proton chain, CNO cycle convert H to He releasing energy that powers stars.
• Interstellar medium contains vast reservoirs of cold H I clouds detectable through 21‑cm line. | | **Environmental/Safety Notes** | • Extremely flammable; explosion limits 4 %–75 % H₂ in air.
• Ignition temperature ~500 °C (varies with concentration).
• No colour, smell, taste – requires sensors for leak detection.
